moment: searching the client's own spell table by TYPE — the in-game Actions window's Category and Subcategory columns, in the app
source: JOS-507 (boundary verdict 7's second question; not a plan-doc moment — the four numbered moments are 01-04)
note: THE OWNER'S SCREENSHOT IS THE SPECIFICATION: a `tap` search over a SHD/BRD/WIZ combo returning every tap by level, filed under Category `Taps` and Subcategory `Health` / `Duration Tap` / `Power Tap`. The app can offer this because the player's own install states it — `spells_us.txt` files every spell under two integer ids (fields 86 and 87, verified against that install) and `dbstr_us.txt` type 5 says what the ids are called — and the engine reads both, beside the log the attach named. WHAT THIS CONVERSATION SHOWS THAT PROSE CANNOT: the first reply's rows are `Leech` and `Siphon Strength` before `Lifetap`, and NEITHER OF THE FIRST TWO NAMES CONTAINS THE SUBSTRING `tap`. They are in the list because their CATEGORY is `Taps` — that is what searching by TYPE means, and a name-only filter would return the third row alone. The order is level DESCENDING, the game's own, and it ends in the source's own tiebreak so it is total: the corpus is a hash map with randomised iteration, so an order stopping at the level would answer the same query differently on every call. `categories` rides the answer because the app CANNOT ship that list — the vocabulary is Daybreak's and lives only in the player's install — and it describes the class and text scope while deliberately ignoring the category filter it populates, so a control never collapses to the value just picked. The second exchange is the same question asked by TYPE with no text at all, windowed, showing `total` behind a window of two. The last is the state an `EQ_INSTALL_DIR` pointed at a folder of logs produces: `spellTable: missing` with the path it looked at, which is an ANSWER and never an error — and note the field is `spellTable` rather than `table`, because `resist.spell` already owns that word as its discriminator in the app's guard matrix and a second arm carrying it would be a shape that guard could no longer refuse. NO BULK FRAME, EVER: the parsed table is 48,256 entries and 6.13 MiB against an 8 MiB ceiling, so there is a window here and there will never be an op without one.
